comment: The conformance model is strong for component services, roles, transactions and standards coverage, but it does not clearly require tests that clinically significant meaning survives an end-to-end transformation. FHIR validity and transaction success do not by themselves detect lossy mappings, altered status or certainty, missing provenance, or broken relationships between clinical concepts.

public.text: The conformance model is strong for component services, roles, transactions and standards coverage, but it does not clearly require tests that clinically significant meaning survives an end-to-end transformation. FHIR validity and transaction success do not by themselves detect lossy mappings, altered status or certainty, missing provenance, or broken relationships between clinical concepts.
public.suggestedRevision: Extend semantic conformance testing to include preservation of provenance and authorship; status, certainty and negation; mandatory terminology bindings; units and reference systems; relationships among clinical concepts; absent/unknown/not-applicable distinctions; detection of lossy mappings; and professional review of clinically significant transformations. Include these checks in reusable reference test data and regression test packs where feasible.
